chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥammād al-Anṣārī narrated from Sadīr, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said:
“O Abā al-Faḍl, do you not have a place in the market where you sit and deal with the people?” He said: I said, “Yes.” He said:

“Know that there is no man who goes out and returns to his place of sitting and his market, then says when he places his foot in the market: ‘O Allah, I ask You for its good and the good of its people, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of its people,’ except that Allah, Mighty and Exalted, appoints for him one who protects him and guards him until he returns to his home. Then he says to him: ‘I have granted you protection from its evil and the evil of its people on this day of yours.’”

“Then when he sits in his place, as he sits, he says: ‘I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger, صلى الله عليه وآله. O Allah, I ask You from Your bounty for lawful, pure provision, and I seek refuge in You from wronging or being wronged, and I seek refuge in You from a losing transaction and a false oath.’”

“So when he says that, the appointed angel says: ‘Receive glad tidings, for there is no one in your market today with a fuller share than you, and what Allah has apportioned for you will come to you in full—lawful, pure, and blessed therein.’”

key_terms.أَعُوذُ بِكَ: I seek refuge in You for protection from harm
key_terms.السُّوقِ: the marketplace where one conducts dealings with people
key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ: O Allah; the opening invocation of supplication
key_terms.خَيْرَهَا: its good, meaning the benefit and goodness of the market
key_terms.يَمِينٍ كَاذِبَةٍ: a false oath used in dealings

ai.seo_question: What du'a should be recited when entering the market and beginning trade?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a supplication and testimony to be recited upon entering the market and when sitting for trade. It emphasizes seeking Allah’s protection, asking for halal and pure provision, and avoiding ظلم, loss, and false oaths in commercial dealings.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3754 - Abdullah ibn Hammad Al-Ansari narrated from Sadeer, who said: Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said:
"O Abu Al-Fadl, do you not have a place in the market where you sit and deal with people?"
I said: "Yes."

Imam (as) said: "Know that any man who goes to his seat in the market, and when he places his foot in the market says:
'O Allah (swt), I ask You for its goodness and the goodness of its people, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of its people',
Allah (swt), the Mighty and Exalted, appoints an angel to protect him and preserve him until he returns to his home.

The angel then says to him, 'I have safeguarded you from its evil and the evil of its people for this day.'
And when he sits in his place, he should say:
'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt), alone, without any partner. And I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. O Allah (swt), I ask You for lawful, pure sustenance from Your bounty, and I seek refuge in You from wronging others or being wronged, and I seek refuge in You from a bad transaction and a false oath.'
When he says this, the appointed angel says, 'Rejoice!
For there is no one in the market today with a greater share than you. And what Allah (swt) has decreed for you will come to you fully, lawfully, purely, and with blessings.'"
